Enable support for cross-signed certificate verification in the certificate bundle.
This feature uses an internal callback to verify the cross-signed certificates.
This feature is kept disabled by default as enabling this feature increases
heap usage by approximately 700 bytes.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CERTIFICATE_BUNDLE_CROSS_SIGNED_VERIFY
children.title: Support cross-signed certificate verification in certificate bundle

children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_TLS1_3_KEXM_PSK_EPHEMERAL
children.title: TLS 1.3 PSK ephemeral key exchange mode

children.help: Enable support for TLS 1.3 early data (0-RTT).
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_EARLY_DATA
children.title: TLS 1.3 early data

children.help: Provisions for GM/T SSL 1.1 support
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_PROTO_GMTSSL1_1
children.title: Support GM/T SSL 1.1 protocol

children.help:
mbedTLS can be compiled with protocol support for the TLS
server, TLS client, or both server and client.

Reducing the number of TLS roles supported saves code size.
children.name: MBEDTLS_TLS_MODE
children.title: TLS Protocol Role

children.help:
Controls the use of record plaintext padding in TLS 1.3 and
when using the Connection ID extension in DTLS 1.2.

The padding will always be chosen so that the length of the
padded plaintext is a multiple of the value of this option.

Notes:
A value of 1 means that no padding will be used for outgoing records.
On systems lacking division instructions, a power of two should be preferred.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_CID_PADDING_GRANULARITY
children.title: Record plaintext padding

children.help:
Keep the peer's certificate after completion of the handshake.
Disabling this option will save about 4kB of heap and some code size.

See mbedTLS documentation for required API and more details.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_KEEP_PEER_CERTIFICATE
children.title: Keep peer certificate after handshake completion

children.help:
Enable serialization of the TLS context structures
This is a local optimization in handling a single, potentially long-lived connection.

See mbedTLS documentation for required API and more details.
Disabling this option will save some code and RAM size.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_CONTEXT_SERIALIZATION
children.title: Enable serialization of the TLS context structures

children.help: Enable simple SSL session cache implementation.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_CACHE_C
children.title: Enable SSL session cache

children.help:
Enable all TLS alert messages in case of encountered errors as per RFC.
If disabled, Mbed TLS can still communicate with other servers, only debugging of failures is harder.
The advantage of not sending alert messages, is that no information is given about reasons for failures
thus preventing adversaries of gaining intel.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_ALL_ALERT_MESSAGES
children.title: Enable all TLS alert messages

children.help: Enable to support symmetric key PSK (pre-shared-key) TLS key exchange modes.
children.name: MBEDTLS_KEY_EXCHANGE_PSK
children.title: Enable PSK based ciphersuite modes

children.help: Enable to support Diffie-Hellman PSK (pre-shared-key) TLS authentication modes.
children.name: MBEDTLS_KEY_EXCHANGE_DHE_PSK
children.title: Enable DHE-PSK based ciphersuite modes

children.help: Enable to support Elliptic-Curve-Diffie-Hellman PSK (pre-shared-key) TLS authentication modes.
children.name: MBEDTLS_KEY_EXCHANGE_ECDHE_PSK
children.title: Enable ECDHE-PSK based ciphersuite modes

children.help: Enable to support RSA PSK (pre-shared-key) TLS authentication modes.
children.name: MBEDTLS_KEY_EXCHANGE_RSA_PSK
children.title: Enable RSA-PSK based ciphersuite modes

children.help:
Enable to show configuration for different types of pre-shared-key TLS authentatication methods.

Leaving this options disabled will save code size if they are not used.
children.name: MBEDTLS_PSK_MODES
children.title: Enable pre-shared-key ciphersuites

children.help: Enable to support ciphersuites with prefix TLS-RSA-WITH-
children.name: MBEDTLS_KEY_EXCHANGE_RSA
children.title: Enable RSA-only based ciphersuite modes

children.help: Enable to support ciphersuites with prefix TLS-DHE-RSA-WITH-
children.name: MBEDTLS_KEY_EXCHANGE_DHE_RSA
children.title: Enable DHE-RSA based ciphersuite modes

children.help: Enable to support ciphersuites with prefix TLS-ECDHE-RSA-WITH-
children.name: MBEDTLS_KEY_EXCHANGE_ECDHE_RSA
children.title: Enable ECDHE-RSA based ciphersuite modes

children.help: Enable to support ciphersuites with prefix TLS-ECDHE-ECDSA-WITH-
children.name: MBEDTLS_KEY_EXCHANGE_ECDHE_ECDSA
children.title: Enable ECDHE-ECDSA based ciphersuite modes

children.help: Enable to support ciphersuites with prefix TLS-ECDH-ECDSA-WITH-
children.name: MBEDTLS_KEY_EXCHANGE_ECDH_ECDSA
children.title: Enable ECDH-ECDSA based ciphersuite modes

children.help: Enable to support ciphersuites with prefix TLS-ECDH-RSA-WITH-
children.name: MBEDTLS_KEY_EXCHANGE_ECDH_RSA
children.title: Enable ECDH-RSA based ciphersuite modes

children.help:
Enable to show Elliptic Curve based ciphersuite mode options.
Disabling all Elliptic Curve ciphersuites saves code size and
can give slightly faster TLS handshakes, provided the server supports
RSA-only ciphersuite modes.
children.name: MBEDTLS_KEY_EXCHANGE_ELLIPTIC_CURVE
children.title: Support Elliptic Curve based ciphersuites

children.help: Enable to support ciphersuites with prefix TLS-ECJPAKE-WITH-
children.name: MBEDTLS_KEY_EXCHANGE_ECJPAKE
children.title: Enable ECJPAKE based ciphersuite modes

children.help: Enable support for RFC 6066 server name indication (SNI).
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_SERVER_NAME_INDICATION
children.title: Enable server name indication

children.help: Disabling this option will save some code size if it is not needed.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_ALPN
children.title: Support ALPN (Application Layer Protocol Negotiation)

children.help: Enable support for the TLS max fragment length extension.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_MAX_FRAGMENT_LENGTH
children.title: Enable support for TLS max fragment length extension

children.help: Enable support for record size limit in TLS 1.3.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_RECORD_SIZE_LIMIT
children.title: Enable support for record size limit

children.help:
This enables the SSL buffer to be resized automatically
based on the negotiated maximum fragment length in each direction.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_VARIABLE_BUFFER_LENGTH
children.title: Variable SSL buffer length

children.help:
The two main uses of renegotiation are (1) refresh keys on long-lived
connections and (2) client authentication after the initial handshake.
If you don't need renegotiation, disabling it will save code size and
reduce the possibility of abuse/vulnerability.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_RENEGOTIATION
children.title: Support TLS renegotiation

children.help:
Client support for RFC 5077 session tickets. See mbedTLS documentation for more details.
Disabling this option will save some code size.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CLIENT_SSL_SESSION_TICKETS
children.title: TLS: Client Support for RFC 5077 SSL session tickets

children.help:
Server support for RFC 5077 session tickets. See mbedTLS documentation for more details.
Disabling this option will save some code size.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SERVER_SSL_SESSION_TICKETS
children.title: TLS: Server Support for RFC 5077 SSL session tickets

children.help:
Enable shared symmetric keys export for TLS sessions using mbedtls_ssl_export_keying_material()
after SSL handshake. The process for deriving the keys is specified in RFC 5705 for TLS 1.2
and in RFC 8446, Section 7.5, for TLS 1.3.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_KEYING_MATERIAL_EXPORT
children.title: Enable keying material export

children.help:
Enable support for the TLS protocol, which is used for secure communication
over networks. This option is required for most secure network protocols,
including HTTPS, FTPS, and others.

If you do not need TLS support, you can disable this option to save code size.
children.name: MBEDTLS_TLS_ENABLED
children.title: Enable TLS protocol support

children.help: Enable basic DTLS cookie implementation for hello verification.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_COOKIE_C
children.title: Enable SSL session cookie

children.help: Maximum length of CIDs used for incoming DTLS messages
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_CID_IN_LEN_MAX
children.title: Maximum length of CIDs used for incoming DTLS messages

children.help: Maximum length of CIDs used for outgoing DTLS messages
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_CID_OUT_LEN_MAX
children.title: Maximum length of CIDs used for outgoing DTLS messages

children.help:
Enable support for the DTLS Connection ID extension which allows to
identify DTLS connections across changes in the underlying transport.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_DTLS_CONNECTION_ID
children.title: Support for the DTLS Connection ID extension

children.help:
Enable support for negotiation of DTLS-SRTP (RFC 5764) through the use_srtp extension.

See mbedTLS documentation for required API and more details.
Disabling this option will save some code size.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_DTLS_SRTP
children.title: Enable support for negotiation of DTLS-SRTP (RFC 5764)

children.help: Requires TLS 1.2 to be enabled for DTLS 1.2
children.name: MBEDTLS_SSL_PROTO_DTLS
children.title: Support DTLS protocol (all versions)

children.help:
Enable the cipher abstraction layer. This enables generic cipher wrappers
for the block ciphers and stream ciphers.
If you are not using the cipher abstraction layer, you can disable this
option to save some code size.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CIPHER_C
children.title: Cipher abstraction layer

children.help: Reduces ROM usage of the Camellia implementation
children.name: MBEDTLS_CAMELLIA_SMALL_MEMORY
children.title: Use small memory implementation of Camellia

children.help:
Enables the DES block cipher to support 3DES-based TLS ciphersuites.

3DES is vulnerable to the Sweet32 attack and should only be enabled
if absolutely necessary.
children.name: MBEDTLS_DES_C
children.title: DES block cipher (legacy, insecure)

children.help:
Enables the Blowfish block cipher (not used for TLS sessions.)

The Blowfish cipher is not used for mbedTLS TLS sessions but can be
used for other purposes. Read up on the limitations of Blowfish (including
Sweet32) before enabling.
children.name: MBEDTLS_BLOWFISH_C
children.title: Blowfish block cipher (read help)

children.help: Enables the XTEA block cipher.
children.name: MBEDTLS_XTEA_C
children.title: XTEA block cipher

children.help:
Enable Counter with CBC-MAC (CCM) modes for AES and/or Camellia ciphers.

Disabling this option saves some code size.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CCM_C
children.title: CCM (Counter with CBC-MAC) block cipher modes

children.help: Enable Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) modes for AES and/or Camellia ciphers.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CIPHER_MODE_CBC
children.title: CBC (Cipher Block Chaining) block cipher modes

children.help: Enable Cipher Feedback (CFB) modes for AES and/or Camellia ciphers.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CIPHER_MODE_CFB
children.title: CFB (Cipher Feedback) block cipher modes

children.help: Enable Counter (CTR) modes for AES and/or Camellia ciphers.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CIPHER_MODE_CTR
children.title: CTR (Counter) block cipher modes

children.help: Enable Output Feedback (OFB) modes for AES and/or Camellia ciphers.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CIPHER_MODE_OFB
children.title: OFB (Output Feedback) block cipher modes

children.help:
Enable XEX Tweakable Block Cipher with Ciphertext Stealing (XTS) modes
for AES and/or Camellia ciphers.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CIPHER_MODE_XTS
children.title: XTS (XEX Tweakable Block Cipher with Ciphertext Stealing) block cipher modes

children.help:
Enable Galois/Counter Mode for AES and/or Camellia ciphers.

This option is generally faster than CCM.
children.name: MBEDTLS_GCM_C
children.title: GCM (Galois/Counter) block cipher modes

children.help: Enable NIST key wrapping and key wrapping padding.
children.name: MBEDTLS_NIST_KW_C
children.title: NIST key wrapping (KW) and KW padding (KWP)

children.help: Enable PKCS#7 padding for block ciphers.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CIPHER_PADDING_PKCS7
children.title: PKCS#7 padding

children.help: Enable one and zeros padding for block ciphers.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CIPHER_PADDING_ONE_AND_ZEROS
children.title: One and zeros padding

children.help: Enable zeros and length padding for block ciphers.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CIPHER_PADDING_ZEROS_AND_LEN
children.title: Zeros and length padding

children.help: Enable zeros padding for block ciphers.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CIPHER_PADDING_ZEROS
children.title: Zeros padding

children.help:
Enable padding for block ciphers.

Padding is only used for block ciphers in CBC, CFB, CTR and OFB modes.
If you are using a stream cipher or a block cipher in ECB mode, you can
disable this option to save code size.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CIPHER_PADDING
children.title: Cipher padding

children.help:
Store the AES tables in ROM instead of generating them at runtime.
Using precomputed ROM tables reduces RAM usage, but increases
flash usage.
children.name: MBEDTLS_AES_ROM_TABLES
children.title: Store AES tables in ROM

children.help:
Use fewer AES tables to reduce ROM/RAM usage.
Using fewer tables increases the time taken to generate the tables
at runtime, but reduces ROM/RAM usage.
children.name: MBEDTLS_AES_FEWER_TABLES
children.title: Use fewer AES tables

children.help:
Only support 128-bit AES keys.
This reduces code size, but disables support for 192-bit and
256-bit AES keys.
children.name: MBEDTLS_AES_ONLY_128_BIT_KEY_LENGTH
children.title: Only support 128-bit AES keys

children.help:
Enable the CMAC (Cipher-based Message Authentication Code) mode for
block ciphers.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CMAC_C
children.title: Enable CMAC mode for block ciphers

children.help: Enable prime number generation.
children.name: MBEDTLS_GENPRIME
children.title: Enable hardware prime number generation

children.help:
Enable support for multiple precision integer (bignum) operations.

This is required for RSA, DSA, DHM, ECDH and ECDSA.

If you don't need any of these algorithms, you can disable this option
to save code size.
children.name: MBEDTLS_BIGNUM_C
children.title: Enable multiple precision integer (bignum) support

children.help: Enable RSA. Needed to use RSA-xxx TLS ciphersuites.
children.name: MBEDTLS_RSA_C
children.title: RSA public key cryptosystem

children.help: Enable support for SECP192R1 Elliptic Curve.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_SECP192R1_ENABLED
children.title: Enable SECP192R1 curve

children.help: Enable support for SECP224R1 Elliptic Curve.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_SECP224R1_ENABLED
children.title: Enable SECP224R1 curve

children.help: Enable support for SECP256R1 Elliptic Curve.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_SECP256R1_ENABLED
children.title: Enable SECP256R1 curve

children.help: Enable support for SECP384R1 Elliptic Curve.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_SECP384R1_ENABLED
children.title: Enable SECP384R1 curve

children.help: Enable support for SECP521R1 Elliptic Curve.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_SECP521R1_ENABLED
children.title: Enable SECP521R1 curve

children.help: Enable support for SECP192K1 Elliptic Curve.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_SECP192K1_ENABLED
children.title: Enable SECP192K1 curve

children.help: Enable support for SECP224K1 Elliptic Curve.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_SECP224K1_ENABLED
children.title: Enable SECP224K1 curve

children.help: Enable support for SECP256K1 Elliptic Curve.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_SECP256K1_ENABLED
children.title: Enable SECP256K1 curve

children.help: support for DP Elliptic Curve.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_BP256R1_ENABLED
children.title: Enable BP256R1 curve

children.help: support for DP Elliptic Curve.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_BP384R1_ENABLED
children.title: Enable BP384R1 curve

children.help: support for DP Elliptic Curve.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_BP512R1_ENABLED
children.title: Enable BP512R1 curve

children.help: Enable support for CURVE25519 Elliptic Curve.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_CURVE25519_ENABLED
children.title: Enable CURVE25519 curve

children.help:
NIST 'modulo p' optimisations increase Elliptic Curve operation performance.

Disabling this option saves some code size.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_NIST_OPTIM
children.title: NIST 'modulo p' optimisations

children.help:
This configuration option enables optimizations to speedup (about 3 ~ 4 times) the ECP
fixed point multiplication using pre-computed tables in the flash memory.
Enabling this configuration option increases the flash footprint
(about 29KB if all Elliptic Curve selected) in the application binary.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_FIXED_POINT_OPTIM
children.title: Enable fixed-point multiplication optimisations

children.help:
Use the legacy ECDH context format.
Define this option only if you enable MBEDTLS_ECP_RESTARTABLE or if you
want to access ECDH context fields directly.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECDH_LEGACY_CONTEXT
children.title: Use a backward compatible ECDH context (Experimental)

children.help:
Enable DHM. Needed to use DHE-xxx TLS ciphersuites.

Note that the security of Diffie-Hellman key exchanges depends on
a suitable prime being used for the exchange. Please see detailed
warning text about this in file `mbedtls/dhm.h` file.
children.name: MBEDTLS_DHM_C
children.title: Diffie-Hellman-Merkle key exchange (DHM)

children.help: Enable ECDH. Needed to use ECDHE-xxx TLS ciphersuites.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECDH_C
children.title: Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH)

children.help: Enable ECJPAKE. Needed to use ECJPAKE-xxx TLS ciphersuites.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECJPAKE_C
children.title: Elliptic curve J-PAKE

children.help: Enable ECDSA. Needed to use ECDSA-xxx TLS ciphersuites.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECDSA_C
children.title: Elliptic Curve DSA

children.help:
Enhance support for reading EC keys using variants of SEC1 not allowed by
RFC 5915 and RFC 5480.
children.name: MBEDTLS_PK_PARSE_EC_EXTENDED
children.title: Enhance support for reading EC keys

children.help:
Enable the support for parsing public keys of type Short Weierstrass
(MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_SECP_XXX and MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_BP_XXX) which are using the
compressed point format. This parsing is done through ECP module's functions.
depends on MBEDTLS_ECP_C
children.name: MBEDTLS_PK_PARSE_EC_COMPRESSED
children.title: Enable the support for parsing public keys of type Short Weierstrass

children.help:
Standard ECDSA is "fragile" in the sense that lack of entropy when signing
may result in a compromise of the long-term signing key.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECDSA_DETERMINISTIC
children.title: Enable deterministic ECDSA

children.help: Enable "non-blocking" ECC operations that can return early and be resumed.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECP_RESTARTABLE
children.title: Enable mbedTLS ecp restartable

children.help:
Enable support for the Hashed Message Authentication Code
(HMAC)-based key derivation function (HKDF).
children.name: MBEDTLS_HKDF_C
children.title: HKDF algorithm (RFC 5869)

children.help: Enable support for Poly1305 MAC algorithm.
children.name: MBEDTLS_POLY1305_C
children.title: Poly1305 MAC algorithm

children.help: Enable the RIPEMD-160 hash algorithm.
children.name: MBEDTLS_RIPEMD160_C
children.title: Enable RIPEMD-160 hash algorithm

children.depends_on: MBEDTLS_MD5_C || MBEDTLS_RIPEMD160_C || MBEDTLS_SHA1_C || MBEDTLS_SHA224_C || MBEDTLS_SHA256_C || MBEDTLS_SHA384_C || MBEDTLS_SHA512_C
children.help: Enable generic layer for message digest algorithms.
children.name: MBEDTLS_MD_C
children.title: Enable message digest support

children.help:
Enables support for MD5.
This module is required for TLS 1.2 depending on the handshake parameters.
Further, it is used for checking MD5-signed certificates, and for PBKDF1
when decrypting PEM-encoded encrypted keys.
MD5 is considered a weak message digest and its use constitutes
a security risk. If possible, consider stronger message digests
such as SHA-256 (part of the SHA-2 family).
children.name: MBEDTLS_MD5_C
children.title: Enable the MD5 cryptographic hash algorithm

children.help:
Enabling MBEDTLS_SHA1_C adds support for SHA-1.
SHA-1 is considered a weak message digest and its use constitutes
a security risk.
Disabling this configuration option could impact TLS 1.2 / Wi-Fi Enterprise compatibility
with certain older certificates that rely on SHA-1 for digital signatures.
Before proceeding, ensure that all your certificates are using stronger hash algorithms,
such as SHA-256 (part of the SHA-2 family).
If you're using older certificates or if you're unsure about the impact on your product,
please consider testing the changes in a controlled environment for individual features
like OTA updates, cloud connectivity, secure local control, etc.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SHA1_C
children.title: Enable the SHA-1 cryptographic hash algorithm

children.help: Enable MBEDTLS_SHA224_C adds support for SHA-224.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SHA224_C
children.title: Enable the SHA-224 cryptographic hash algorithm

children.help: Enable MBEDTLS_SHA256_C adds support for SHA-256.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SHA256_C
children.title: Enable the SHA-256 cryptographic hash algorithm

children.help: Enable MBEDTLS_SHA384_C adds support for SHA-384.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SHA384_C
children.title: Enable the SHA-384 cryptographic hash algorithm

children.help: Enable MBEDTLS_SHA512_C adds support for SHA-512.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SHA512_C
children.title: Enable the SHA-384 and SHA-512 cryptographic hash algorithms

children.help:
Enabling MBEDTLS_SHA3_C adds support for SHA3.
Enabling this configuration option increases the flash footprint
by almost 4KB.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SHA3_C
children.title: Enable the SHA3 cryptographic hash algorithm

children.help: Use ROM MD5 in mbedTLS.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ROM_MD5
children.title: Use MD5 implementation in ROM

children.help:
Enable a smaller implementation of SHA-256 that has lower ROM footprint
but is slower than the default implementation.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SHA256_SMALLER
children.title: Enable SHA-256 smaller implementation

children.help:
Enable a smaller implementation of SHA-512 that has lower ROM footprint
but is slower than the default implementation.
children.name: MBEDTLS_SHA512_SMALLER
children.title: Enable SHA-512 smaller implementation

children.help:
Enable hardware accelerated ECDSA peripheral to verify signature
on curve SECP192R1 and SECP256R1 in mbedTLS.
children.name: MBEDTLS_HARDWARE_ECDSA_VERIFY
children.title: Enable ECDSA signature verification using on-chip ECDSA peripheral

children.help:
The ECDSA peripheral before ESP32-H2 v1.2 does not offer constant time ECDSA sign operation.
This time can be observed through power profiling of the device,
making the ECDSA private key vulnerable to side-channel timing attacks.
This countermeasure masks the real ECDSA sign operation
under dummy sign operations to add randomness in the generated power signature.
It is highly recommended to also enable Secure Boot for the device
in addition to this countermeasure so that only trusted software can execute on the device.
This countermeasure can be safely disabled for ESP32-H2 v1.2 and above.
children.name: MBEDTLS_HARDWARE_ECDSA_SIGN_MASKING_CM
children.title: Mask original ECDSA sign operation under dummy sign operations

children.help:
This option adds a delay after the actual ECDSA signature operation
so that the entire operation appears to be constant  time for the software.
This fix helps in protecting the device only in case of remote timing attack
on the ECDSA private key.
For e.g., When an interface is exposed by the device to perform ECDSA signature
of an arbitrary message.
The signature time would appear to be constant to the external entity after enabling
this option.
This countermeasure can be safely disabled for ESP32-H2 v1.2 and above.
children.name: MBEDTLS_HARDWARE_ECDSA_SIGN_CONSTANT_TIME_CM
children.title: Make ECDSA signature operation pseudo constant time for software
Enable Software Countermeasure for ECDSA signing using on-chip ECDSA peripheral

children.help:
Enable hardware accelerated ECDSA peripheral to sign data
on curve SECP192R1 and SECP256R1 in mbedTLS.

Note that for signing, the private key has to be burnt in an efuse key block
with key purpose set to ECDSA_KEY.
If no key is burnt, it will report an error

The key should be burnt in little endian format. espefuse utility handles it internally
but care needs to be taken while burning using esp_efuse APIs
children.name: MBEDTLS_HARDWARE_ECDSA_SIGN
children.title: Enable ECDSA signing using on-chip ECDSA peripheral

children.name: MBEDTLS_TEE_SEC_STG_ECDSA_SIGN
children.title: Enable ECDSA signing using TEE secure storage

children.help:
Fallback to software implementation of ECC point multiplication and point verification
for curves not supported in hardware.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ECC_OTHER_CURVES_SOFT_FALLBACK
children.title: Fallback to software implementation for curves not supported in hardware

children.help:
Enable hardware accelerated ECC point multiplication and point verification for points
on curve SECP192R1 and SECP256R1 in mbedTLS
children.name: MBEDTLS_HARDWARE_ECC
children.title: Enable hardware ECC acceleration

children.help:
Enable hardware accelerated SHA1, SHA256, SHA384 & SHA512 in mbedTLS.

Due to a hardware limitation, on the ESP32 hardware acceleration is only
guaranteed if SHA digests are calculated one at a time. If more
than one SHA digest is calculated at the same time, one will
be calculated fully in hardware and the rest will be calculated
(at least partially calculated) in software. This happens automatically.

SHA hardware acceleration is faster than software in some situations but
slower in others. You should benchmark to find the best setting for you.
children.name: MBEDTLS_HARDWARE_SHA
children.title: Enable hardware SHA acceleration

children.help:
Fallback to software implementation for RSA key lengths
larger than SOC_RSA_MAX_BIT_LEN. If this is not active
then the ESP will be unable to process keys greater
than SOC_RSA_MAX_BIT_LEN.
children.name: MBEDTLS_LARGE_KEY_SOFTWARE_MPI
children.title: Fallback to software implementation for larger MPI values

children.help:
This config helps to set the interrupt priority level for the MPI peripheral.
Value 0 (default) means that there is no preference regarding the interrupt
priority level and any level from 1 to 3 can be selected (based on the availability).
Note: Higher value indicates high interrupt priority.
children.name: MBEDTLS_MPI_INTERRUPT_LEVEL
children.title: MPI hardware interrupt level

children.help:
Use an interrupt to coordinate long MPI operations.

This allows other code to run on the CPU while an MPI operation is pending.
Otherwise the CPU busy-waits.
children.name: MBEDTLS_MPI_USE_INTERRUPT
children.title: Use interrupt for MPI exp-mod operations

children.help:
Enable hardware accelerated multiple precision integer operations.

Hardware accelerated multiplication, modulo multiplication,
and modular exponentiation for up to SOC_RSA_MAX_BIT_LEN bit results.

These operations are used by RSA.
children.name: MBEDTLS_HARDWARE_MPI
children.title: Enable hardware MPI (bignum) acceleration

children.help:
Enable partially hardware accelerated GCM. GHASH calculation is still done
in software.

If MBEDTLS_HARDWARE_GCM is disabled and MBEDTLS_HARDWARE_AES is enabled then
mbedTLS will still use the hardware accelerated AES block operation, but
on a single block at a time.
children.name: MBEDTLS_HARDWARE_GCM
children.title: Enable partially hardware accelerated GCM

children.help:
Enable this config to support fallback to software definitions for a non-AES
cipher GCM operation as we support hardware acceleration only for AES cipher.
Some of the non-AES ciphers used in a GCM operation are DES, ARIA, CAMELLIA,
CHACHA20, BLOWFISH.

If this config is disabled, performing a non-AES cipher GCM operation with
the config MBEDTLS_HARDWARE_AES enabled will result in calculation of an
AES-GCM operation instead for the given input values and thus could lead
to failure in certificate validation which would ultimately lead to a SSL
handshake failure.

This config being by-default enabled leads to an increase in binary size
footprint of ~2.5KB.
In case you are sure that your use case (for example, client and server
settings in case of a TLS handshake) would not involve any GCM
operations using a non-AES cipher, you can safely disable this config,
leading to reduction in binary size footprint.
children.name: MBEDTLS_GCM_SUPPORT_NON_AES_CIPHER
children.title: Enable support for non-AES ciphers in GCM operation

children.help:
This config helps to set the interrupt priority level for the AES peripheral.
Value 0 (default) means that there is no preference regarding the interrupt
priority level and any level from 1 to 3 can be selected (based on the availability).
Note: Higher value indicates high interrupt priority.
children.name: MBEDTLS_AES_INTERRUPT_LEVEL
children.title: AES hardware interrupt level

children.help:
Use an interrupt to coordinate long AES operations.

This allows other code to run on the CPU while an AES operation is pending.
Otherwise the CPU busy-waits.
children.name: MBEDTLS_AES_USE_INTERRUPT
children.title: Use interrupt for long AES operations

children.help:
The strength of the pseudo rounds functions can be configured to low, medium and high.
You can configure the strength of the pseudo rounds functions according to your use cases,
for example, increasing the strength would provide higher security but would slow down the
hardware AES encryption/decryption operations.
children.name: MBEDTLS_AES_USE_PSEUDO_ROUND_FUNC_STRENGTH
children.title: Strength of the pseudo rounds function

children.help:
Enables the pseudo round function of the AES peripheral.
Enabling this would impact the performance of the AES operations.
For more info regarding the performance impact, please checkout
the pseudo round function section of the security guide.
children.name: MBEDTLS_AES_USE_PSEUDO_ROUND_FUNC
children.title: Enable AES hardware's pseudo round function

children.help:
Enable hardware accelerated AES encryption & decryption.

Note that if the ESP32 CPU is running at 240MHz, hardware AES does not
offer any speed boost over software AES.
children.name: MBEDTLS_HARDWARE_AES
children.title: Enable hardware AES acceleration

children.help:
This option enables dynamically switching between the hardware
AES peripheral's block and DMA modes based on the length of the input data,
thus, significantly speeding up the AES operations with shorter data lengths.
For example, NVS encryption/decryption operations, TLS communication, etc.
with smaller data lengths.

It is enabled by default due to the significant performance impact but note that
it also increases the binary size by ~1.2 KB as it pulls in the peripheral's block
mode code as well.
children.name: MBEDTLS_AES_HW_SMALL_DATA_LEN_OPTIM
children.title: Enable performance optimisation for the small data length hardware AES operations

children.help: Support external private RSA keys (eg from a HSM) int the PK layer.
children.name: MBEDTLS_PK_RSA_ALT_SUPPORT
children.title: Enable RSA alt support

children.help:
This option enables hardware acceleration for ECDSA sign function, only
when using ATECC608A cryptoauth chip.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ATCA_HW_ECDSA_SIGN
children.title: Enable hardware ECDSA sign acceleration when using ATECC608A

children.help:
This option enables hardware acceleration for ECDSA sign function, only
when using ATECC608A cryptoauth chip.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ATCA_HW_ECDSA_VERIFY
children.title: Enable hardware ECDSA verify acceleration when using ATECC608A

children.help:
Enable support for entropy sources and provides a generic
entropy pool.
children.name: MBEDTLS_ENTROPY_C
children.title: Enable entropy support

children.help:
Force SHA-256 to be used for the entropy pool if both SHA-256 and SHA-512 are
enabled. On 32-bit architectures, SHA-256 can be faster than SHA-512
children.name: MBEDTLS_ENTROPY_FORCE_SHA256
children.title: Force SHA-256 for entropy

children.help:
Enable CTR_DRBG (CTR mode Deterministic Random Bit Generator).
The CTR_DRBG generator uses AES-256 by default.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CTR_DRBG_C
children.title: Enable CTR_DRBG

children.help: Enable HMAC_DRBG (HMAC mode Deterministic Random Bit Generator).
children.name: MBEDTLS_HMAC_DRBG_C
children.title: Enable HMAC_DRBG

children.help: Enable Base64 encoding and decoding functions. This is required for PEM support.
children.name: MBEDTLS_BASE64_C
children.title: Enable Base64 encoding/decoding

children.help: Enable support for PKCS#5 functions.
children.name: MBEDTLS_PKCS5_C
children.title: Enable PKCS#5 functions

children.depends_on: MBEDTLS_ASN1_PARSE_C && MBEDTLS_OID_C && MBEDTLS_PK_PARSE_C && MBEDTLS_X509_CRT_PARSE_C && MBEDTLS_X509_CRL_PARSE_C && MBEDTLS_BIGNUM_C && MBEDTLS_MD_C
children.help: Enable PKCS number 7 core for using PKCS number 7-formatted signatures.
children.name: MBEDTLS_PKCS7_C
children.title: Enable PKCS number 7

children.help: Enable PKCS number 12 core for using PKCS number 12-formatted signatures.
children.name: MBEDTLS_PKCS12_C
children.title: Enable PKCS number 12

children.help: Enable support for PKCS#1 v1.5 operations.
children.name: MBEDTLS_PKCS1_V15
children.title: Enable PKCS#1 v1.5 padding

children.help: Enable support for PKCS#1 v2.1 operations.
children.name: MBEDTLS_PKCS1_V21
children.title: Enable PKCS#1 v2.1 padding

children.help: Enable support for ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD algorithm.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CHACHAPOLY_C
children.title: ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD algorithm

children.help: Enable support for Chacha20 stream cipher.
children.name: MBEDTLS_CHACHA20_C
children.title: Chacha20 stream cipher

children.help:
Enable this flag to use mbedtls crypto algorithm from ROM instead of ESP-IDF
in case of a bootloader build.
Similar to the MBEDTLS_USE_CRYPTO_ROM_IMPL config but enables usage of the
mbedtls crypto algorithm from ROM for the bootloader build.
children.name: MBEDTLS_USE_CRYPTO_ROM_IMPL_BOOTLOADER
children.title: Use ROM implementation of the crypto algorithm in the bootloader

children.help:
Enable this flag to use mbedtls crypto algorithm from ROM instead of ESP-IDF.

This configuration option saves flash footprint in the application binary.
Note that the version of mbedtls crypto algorithm library in ROM(ECO1~ECO3) is v2.16.12,
and the version of mbedtls crypto algorithm library in ROM(ECO4) is v3.6.0.
We have done the security analysis of the mbedtls revision in ROM (ECO1~ECO4)
and ensured that affected symbols have been patched (removed). If in the future
mbedtls revisions there are security issues that also affects the version in
ROM (ECO1~ECO4) then we shall patch the relevant symbols. This would increase
the flash footprint and hence care must be taken to keep some reserved space
for the application binary in flash layout.
children.name: MBEDTLS_USE_CRYPTO_ROM_IMPL
children.title: Use ROM implementation of the crypto algorithm

children.help:
This option enables encryption for NVS. When enabled, XTS-AES is used to encrypt
the complete NVS data, except the page headers. It requires XTS encryption keys
to be stored in an encrypted partition (enabling flash encryption is mandatory here)
or to be derived from an HMAC key burnt in eFuse.
children.name: NVS_ENCRYPTION
children.title: Enable NVS encryption

children.help:
Enabling this will ignore "encrypted" flag for NVS partitions. NVS encryption
scheme is different than hardware flash encryption and hence it is not recommended
to have "encrypted" flag for NVS partitions. This was not being checked in pre v4.3
IDF. Hence, if you have any devices where this flag is kept enabled in partition
table then enabling this config will allow to have same behavior as pre v4.3 IDF.
children.name: NVS_COMPATIBLE_PRE_V4_3_ENCRYPTION_FLAG
children.title: NVS partition encrypted flag compatible with ESP-IDF before v4.3

children.help: This option switches error checking type between assertions (y) or return codes (n).
children.name: NVS_ASSERT_ERROR_CHECK
children.title: Use assertions for error checking

children.help:
Enabling this option will switch the nvs_set() family of functions to the legacy mode:
when called repeatedly with the same key but different data type, the existing value
in the NVS remains active and the new value is just stored, actually not accessible through
corresponding nvs_get() call for the key given. Use this option only when your application
relies on such NVS API behaviour.
children.name: NVS_LEGACY_DUP_KEYS_COMPATIBILITY
children.title: Enable legacy nvs_set function behavior when same key is reused with different data types

children.help:
Enabling this option lets NVS library try to allocate page cache and key hash list in SPIRAM
instead of internal RAM. It can help applications using large nvs partitions or large number
of keys to save heap space in internal RAM. SPIRAM heap allocation negatively impacts speed
of NVS operations as the CPU accesses NVS cache via SPI instead of direct access to the internal RAM.
children.name: NVS_ALLOCATE_CACHE_IN_SPIRAM
children.title: Prefers allocation of in-memory cache structures in SPI connected PSRAM

children.help: This option enforces internal use of Block Device Layer instead ESP_Partition.
children.name: NVS_BDL_STACK
children.title: Run NVS on BDL instead of ESP_Partition

children.help:
Protect the NVS Encryption Keys using Flash Encryption
Requires a separate 'nvs_keys' partition (which will be encrypted by flash encryption)
for storing the NVS encryption keys
children.name: NVS_SEC_KEY_PROTECT_USING_FLASH_ENC
children.title: Using Flash Encryption

children.help:
Derive and protect the NVS Encryption Keys using the HMAC peripheral
Requires the specified eFuse block (NVS_SEC_HMAC_EFUSE_KEY_ID or the v2 API argument)
to be empty or pre-written with a key with the purpose ESP_EFUSE_KEY_PURPOSE_HMAC_UP
children.name: NVS_SEC_KEY_PROTECT_USING_HMAC
children.title: Using HMAC peripheral

children.help:
Select this option if key derivation/protection is handled by
a custom implementation, and not by the nvs_sec_provider component.
children.name: NVS_SEC_KEY_PROTECT_NONE
children.title: None

children.help:
This choice defines the default NVS encryption keys protection scheme;
which will be used for the default NVS partition.
Users can use the corresponding scheme registration APIs to register other
schemes for the default as well as other NVS partitions.
children.name: NVS_SEC_KEY_PROTECTION_SCHEME
children.title: NVS Encryption: Key Protection Scheme

children.help:
eFuse block key ID storing the HMAC key for deriving the NVS encryption keys

Note: The eFuse block key ID required by the HMAC scheme
(CONFIG_NVS_SEC_KEY_PROTECT_USING_HMAC) is set using this config when the default
NVS partition is initialized with nvs_flash_init(). The eFuse block key ID can
also be set at runtime by passing the appropriate value to the NVS security scheme
registration APIs.
children.name: NVS_SEC_HMAC_EFUSE_KEY_ID
children.title: eFuse key ID storing the HMAC key

children.name: OPENTHREAD_CONSOLE_TYPE

children.help:
Enable the OpenThread-specific console provided by the SDK. This only controls whether
the SDK sets up a dedicated console for OpenThread. Even if disabled, the default
ESP-IDF console (if initialized elsewhere) can still be used independently.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_CONSOLE_ENABLE
children.title: Enable OpenThread console

children.help: Select this option to enable Command-Line Interface in OpenThread.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_CLI
children.title: Enable Openthread Command-Line Interface

children.help:
A prefix string used before a Thread CLI command, allowing the ESP console to identify
it and delegate the remaining command to the OpenThread callback for processing.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_CONSOLE_COMMAND_PREFIX
children.title: The prefix of the openthread CLI command registered on the esp console

children.help:
A string in the format "<address>/<plen>", where `<address>` is an IPv6
address and `<plen>` is a prefix length. For example "fd00:db8:a0:0::/64"
children.name: OPENTHREAD_MESH_LOCAL_PREFIX
children.title: OpenThread mesh local prefix, format <address>/<plen>

children.help: The OpenThread network extended pan id in hex string format
children.name: OPENTHREAD_NETWORK_EXTPANID
children.title: OpenThread extended pan id

children.help: The OpenThread network network key in hex string format
children.name: OPENTHREAD_NETWORK_MASTERKEY
children.title: OpenThread network key

children.help: The OpenThread pre-shared commissioner key in hex string format
children.name: OPENTHREAD_NETWORK_PSKC
children.title: OpenThread pre-shared commissioner key

children.help: Select this to enable Full Thread Device which can act as router and leader in a Thread network.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_FTD
children.title: Full Thread Device

children.help:
Select this to enable Minimal Thread Device which can only act as end device in a Thread network.
This will reduce the code size of the OpenThread stack.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_MTD
children.title: Minimal Thread Device

children.help:
Select this to enable Radio Only Device which can only forward 15.4 packets to the host.
The OpenThread stack will be run on the host and OpenThread will have minimal footprint on the
radio only device.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_RADIO
children.title: Radio Only Device

children.help: OpenThread can be configured to different device types (FTD, MTD, Radio)
children.name: OPENTHREAD_DEVICE_TYPE
children.title: Thread device type

children.help: Configure the port number of TREL service.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_TREL_PORT
children.title: The port of openthread trel service

children.help: Configure the receive buffer size of TREL service.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_TREL_BUFFER_SIZE
children.title: The receive buffer size of openthread trel

children.help: Select this option to enable Thread Radio Encapsulation Link.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_RADIO_TREL
children.title: Enable Thread Radio Encapsulation Link (TREL)

children.help: Select this to use the native 15.4 radio.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_RADIO_NATIVE
children.title: Native 15.4 radio

children.help: Select this to connect to a Radio Co-Processor via UART.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_RADIO_SPINEL_UART
children.title: Connect via UART

children.help: Select this to connect to a Radio Co-Processor via SPI.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_RADIO_SPINEL_SPI
children.title: Connect via SPI

children.help: Select this to disable the Thread radio based on 15.4 link.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_RADIO_154_NONE
children.title: Disable the Thread radio based on 15.4 link

children.help: Configure how OpenThread connects to the 15.4 radio
children.name: OPENTHREAD_RADIO_TYPE
children.title: Config the Thread radio type with 15.4 link

children.help: Select this to enable UART connection to host.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_RCP_UART
children.title: UART RCP

children.help: Select this to enable SPI connection to host.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_RCP_SPI
children.title: SPI RCP

children.help: Select this to enable connection to host over USB JTAG serial.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_RCP_USB_SERIAL_JTAG
children.title: USB RCP

children.help: Select this to enable OpenThread NCP vendor commands.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_NCP_VENDOR_HOOK
children.title: Enable vendor command for RCP

children.help: Select this option to enable border router features in OpenThread.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_BORDER_ROUTER
children.title: Enable Border Router

children.name: OPENTHREAD_COMM_MAX_JOINER_ENTRIES
children.title: The size of max commissioning joiner entries

children.help:
Select this option to enable commissioner in OpenThread. This will enable the device to act as a
commissioner in the Thread network. A commissioner checks the pre-shared key from a joining device
with the Thread commissioning protocol and shares the network parameter with the joining device
upon success.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_COMMISSIONER
children.title: Enable Commissioner

children.help:
Select this option to enable Joiner in OpenThread. This allows a device to join the
Thread network with a pre-shared key using the Thread commissioning protocol.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_JOINER
children.title: Enable Joiner

children.help: Set the max buffer size of service entries in the SRP client service pool.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_SRP_CLIENT_MAX_SERVICES
children.title: Specifies number of service entries in the SRP client service pool

children.help:
Select this option to enable SRP Client in OpenThread.
This allows a device to register SRP services to SRP Server.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_SRP_CLIENT
children.title: Enable SRP Client

children.help: Select this option to enable DNS Client in OpenThread.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_DNS_CLIENT
children.title: Enable DNS Client

children.help: Set the DNS server IPv4 address.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_DNS_SERVER_ADDR
children.title: DNS server address (IPv4)

children.help: Select this option to acquire NAT64 address from dns servers.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_DNS64_CLIENT
children.title: Enable DNS64 Client

children.help: Select this option to enable timing optimization for link metrics / CSL features.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_TIMING_OPTIMIZATION
children.title: Enable timing optimization

children.help: Select this option to enable link metrics feature
children.name: OPENTHREAD_LINK_METRICS
children.title: Enable link metrics feature

children.help: Select this option to enable border agent feature
children.name: OPENTHREAD_BORDER_AGENT_ENABLE
children.title: Enable border agent feature

commands in the OpenThread command line. These commands allow users to manipulate low-level

children.name: OPENTHREAD_DIAG

children.help:
Select this option to enable "Periodic Parent Search" function for MTD. This checks the average
RSS to its current parent every periodically and starts a parent search process if the average

children.name: OPENTHREAD_PARENT_SEARCH_RESELECT_TIMEOUT_MINS

children.help:
This option allows users to tailor the values of openthread macros according to their requirements.
The openthread submodule contains numerous macros, each with a default value set. In the Kconfig of
ESP openthread, users can set specific openthread parameters, which will be applied for certain
openthread macros in the openthread-core-esp32x-xxx-config.h file. During compilation, the values
specified in openthread-core-esp32x-xxx-config.h will replace the default settings in the openthread
submodule. However, Kconfig does not cover all openthread macros, particularly those typically
using default values. For such macros, users can enable the OPENTHREAD_HEADER_CUSTOM option in the
Kconfig and provide a custom header file. Macros defined in the custom header file will have the
highest priority.
children.name: OPENTHREAD_HEADER_CUSTOM
children.title: Use a header file defined by customer

This includes various diagnostic tools and logs to help track down
issues in OpenThread networking or system integration

children.title: Default name of pthreads

children.help:
When this option is selected, the patch will be enabled for XMC.
Follow the recommended flow by XMC for better stability.

DO NOT DISABLE UNLESS YOU KNOW WHAT YOU ARE DOING.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_BROWNOUT_RESET_XMC
children.title: Enable sending reset when brownout for XMC flash chips

children.help:
When brownout happens during flash erase/write operations,
send reset command to stop the flash operations to improve stability.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_BROWNOUT_RESET

children.help: This is a helper config for HPM. Invisible for users.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_UNDER_HIGH_FREQ

children.help:
Whether the High Performance Mode of Flash is enabled. As an optional feature, user needs to manually
enable this option as a confirmation. To be back-compatible with earlier IDF version, this option is
automatically enabled with warning when Flash running > 80Mhz.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_HPM
children.title: High Performance Mode (READ DOCS FIRST, > 80MHz)

children.help:
This option is invisible, and will be selected automatically
when ``ESPTOOLPY_FLASHFREQ_120M`` is selected.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_HPM_ON

children.help:
This feature needs your bootloader to be compiled DC-aware (BOOTLOADER_FLASH_DC_AWARE=y). Otherwise the
chip will not be able to boot after a reset.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_HPM_DC
children.title: Support HPM using DC (READ DOCS FIRST)

children.help:
This is a helper config for HPM. Whether HPM-DC is enabled is also determined by bootloader.
Invisible for users.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_HPM_DC_ON

children.help:
This option is disabled by default because it is supported only
for specific flash chips and for specific Espressif chips.
To evaluate if you can use this feature refer to
`Optional Features for Flash` > `Auto Suspend & Resume` of the `ESP-IDF Programming Guide`.

CAUTION: If you want to OTA to an app with this feature turned on, please make
sure the bootloader has the support for it. (later than IDF v4.3)

If you are using an official Espressif module, please contact Espressif Business support
to check if the module has the flash that support this feature installed.
Also refer to `Concurrency Constraints for Flash on SPI1` > `Flash Auto Suspend Feature`
before enabling this option.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_AUTO_SUSPEND
children.title: Auto suspend long erase/write operations (READ DOCS FIRST)

children.help:
This config is used for setting Tsus parameter. Tsus means CS# high to next command after
suspend. You can refer to the chapter of AC CHARACTERISTICS of flash datasheet.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_SUSPEND_TSUS_VAL_US
children.title: SPI flash tSUS value (refer to chapter AC CHARACTERISTICS)

children.help:
This config is used for setting Trs parameter. Trs means CS Latency Between Resume And Next Suspend.
You can refer to the chapter of AC CHARACTERISTICS of flash datasheet.
For high-performance scenarios, some flash chips allow this set value to be smaller than the
given value in the datasheet without causing errors in the flash state machine.
When you have any related needs, please contact espressif business team.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_SUSPEND_TRS_VAL_US
children.title: SPI flash tRS value (refer to chapter AC CHARACTERISTICS)

children.help:
XMC-C series is regarded as not qualified for the Suspend feature, since its specification
has a tRS >= 1ms restriction. We strongly do not suggest using it for the Suspend feature.
However, if your product in field has enabled this feature, you may still enable this
config option to keep the legacy behavior.

For new users, DO NOT enable this config.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_FORCE_ENABLE_XMC_C_SUSPEND
children.title: Enable XMC-C series flash chip suspend feature anyway

children.help:
Flash suspend has a defect on ESP32C6 until v0.2 and ESP32H2 until v1.2. If you already use suspend
feature for mass production, you can enable this for bypassing check after knowing the risk.
But if you are new users, or developing new applications, or producing a new batch,
please DO NOT enable this config option.

For more information, please refer to errata or connect to Espressif business support team.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_FORCE_ENABLE_C6_H2_SUSPEND
children.title: Enable chip suspend feature on c6 or h2 anyway (DO NOT ENABLE FOR NEW USERS OR APPLICATIONS)

children.help:
Enable this config will disable auto-resume from hardware. Thus the software will resume the chip
after any higher priority task/interrupt which suspend the chip. The benefit is that the suspend-resume
will not disturb the higher priority task and interrupt.

This currently is only valid on single core chip.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_SOFTWARE_RESUME
children.title: Resume flash program/erase form suspend state by software control

children.help:
Disable freertos task scheduler when CONFIG_SPI_FLASH_AUTO_SUSPEND is enabled.
Thus only interrupt can trigger a suspend. When SPI_FLASH_AUTO_SUSPEND is enabled,
default behavior is not disable the task scheduler, so both interrupt and high priority
task can suspend the erase/program operation. When this option is enabled, task
scheduler is disabled, only interrupt can suspend erase/program operation.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_DISABLE_SCHEDULER_IN_SUSPEND
children.title: Disable task scheduler when suspend is enabled when SPI1 operation is ongoing

children.help:
Majority flash supports to use flash register to judge if flash suspend status is
done or not. So enable this config, the behavior would use flash register WIP bit to judge
whether suspend is valid instead of waiting for a specific long time, which can save a
lot of time and benefit for performance improvement.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_AUTO_CHECK_SUSPEND_STATUS
children.title: Check flash status automatically after flash suspend

children.help:
When disabled, certain functions in `spi_flash` component will be placed into Flash memory
instead of IRAM. Disabling this option will save almost 10KB of IRAM depending on which
functions are used.

When enabled, these functions will be placed in internal RAM, with better performance.

For more information please refer to programming guide.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_PLACE_FUNCTIONS_IN_IRAM
children.title: Place spi_flash operation functions into IRAM
Optional and Experimental Features (READ DOCS FIRST)

children.help:
If this option is enabled, if SPI flash write verification fails then a log error line
will be written with the address, expected & actual values. This can be useful when
debugging hardware SPI flash problems.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_LOG_FAILED_WRITE
children.title: Log errors if verification fails

children.help:
If this option is enabled, any SPI flash write which tries to set zero bits in the flash to
ones will log a warning. Such writes will not result in the requested data appearing identically
in flash once written, as SPI NOR flash can only set bits to one when an entire sector is erased.
After erasing, individual bits can only be written from one to zero.

Note that some software (such as SPIFFS) which is aware of SPI NOR flash may write one bits as an
optimisation, relying on the data in flash becoming a bitwise AND of the new data and any existing data.
Such software will log spurious warnings if this option is enabled.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_WARN_SETTING_ZERO_TO_ONE
children.title: Log warning if writing zero bits to ones

children.help:
If this option is enabled, any time SPI flash is written then the data will be read
back and verified. This can catch hardware problems with SPI flash, or flash which
was not erased before verification.

This will slightly influence the write performance.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_VERIFY_WRITE
children.title: Verify SPI flash writes

children.help:
This option enables the following APIs:

- esp_flash_reset_counters
- esp_flash_dump_counters
- esp_flash_get_counters

These APIs may be used to collect performance data for spi_flash APIs
and to help understand behaviour of libraries which use SPI flash.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_ENABLE_COUNTERS
children.title: Enable operation counters

children.help:
Enable this flag to use new SPI flash driver functions from ROM instead of ESP-IDF.

If keeping this as "n" in your project, you will have less free IRAM.
But you can use all of our flash features.

If making this as "y" in your project, you will increase free IRAM.
But you may miss out on some flash features and support for new flash chips.

Currently the ROM cannot support the following features:

- SPI_FLASH_AUTO_SUSPEND (C3, S3)
children.name: SPI_FLASH_ROM_IMPL
children.title: Use esp_flash implementation in ROM

children.help:
SPI flash APIs can optionally abort or return a failure code
if erasing or writing addresses that fall at the beginning
of flash (covering the bootloader and partition table) or that
overlap the app partition that contains the running app.

It is not recommended to ever write to these regions from an IDF app,
and this check prevents logic errors or corrupted firmware memory from
damaging these regions.

Note that this feature *does not* check calls to the esp_rom_xxx SPI flash
ROM functions. These functions should not be called directly from IDF
applications.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_DANGEROUS_WRITE
children.title: Writing to dangerous flash regions

children.help:
Each SPI bus needs a lock for arbitration among devices. This allows multiple
devices on a same bus, but may reduce the speed of esp_flash driver access to the
main flash chip.

If you only need to use esp_flash driver to access the main flash chip, disable
this option, and the lock will be bypassed on SPI1 bus. Otherwise if extra devices
are needed to attach to SPI1 bus, enable this option.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_SHARE_SPI1_BUS
children.title: Support other devices attached to SPI1 bus

children.help:
Some flash chips can have very high "max" erase times, especially for block erase (32KB or 64KB).
This option allows to bypass "block erase" and always do sector erase commands.
This will be much slower overall in most cases, but improves latency for other code to run.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_BYPASS_BLOCK_ERASE
children.title: Bypass a block erase and always do sector erase

children.help:
If a duration of one erase command is large
then it will yield CPUs after finishing a current command.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_ERASE_YIELD_DURATION_MS
children.title: Duration of erasing to yield CPUs (ms)

children.help: Defines how many ticks will be before returning to continue a erasing.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_ERASE_YIELD_TICKS
children.title: CPU release time (tick) for an erase operation

children.help:
This allows to yield the CPUs between erase commands.
Prevents starvation of other tasks.
Please use this configuration together with ``SPI_FLASH_ERASE_YIELD_DURATION_MS`` and
``SPI_FLASH_ERASE_YIELD_TICKS`` after carefully checking flash datasheet to avoid a
watchdog timeout.
For more information, please check `SPI Flash API` reference documentation
under section `OS Function`.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_YIELD_DURING_ERASE
children.title: Enables yield operation during flash erase

children.help:
Flash write is broken down in terms of multiple (smaller) write operations.
This configuration options helps to set individual write chunk size, smaller
value here ensures that cache (and non-IRAM resident interrupts) remains
disabled for shorter duration.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_WRITE_CHUNK_SIZE
children.title: Flash write chunk size

children.help:
SPI Flash driver uses the flash size configured in bootloader header by default.
Enable this option to override flash size with latest ESPTOOLPY_FLASHSIZE value from
the app header if the size in the bootloader header is incorrect.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_SIZE_OVERRIDE
children.title: Override flash size in bootloader header by ESPTOOLPY_FLASHSIZE

children.help: This option is helpful if you are using a flash chip whose timeout is quite large or unpredictable.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_CHECK_ERASE_TIMEOUT_DISABLED
children.title: Flash timeout checkout disabled

children.help:
This option allows the chip driver list to be customized, instead of using the default list provided by
ESP-IDF.

When this option is enabled, the default list is no longer compiled or linked. Instead, the
`default_registered_chips` structure must be provided by the user.

See example: custom_chip_driver under examples/storage for more details.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_OVERRIDE_CHIP_DRIVER_LIST
children.title: Override default chip driver list

children.help:
Enable this to support auto detection of ISSI chips if chip vendor not directly
given by ``chip_drv`` member of the chip struct. This adds support for variant
chips, however will extend detecting time.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_SUPPORT_ISSI_CHIP
children.title: ISSI

children.help:
Enable this to support auto detection of MXIC chips if chip vendor not directly
given by ``chip_drv`` member of the chip struct. This adds support for variant
chips, however will extend detecting time.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_SUPPORT_MXIC_CHIP
children.title: MXIC

children.help:
Enable this to support auto detection of GD (GigaDevice) chips if chip vendor not
directly given by ``chip_drv`` member of the chip struct. If you are using Wrover
modules, please don't disable this, otherwise your flash may not work in 4-bit
mode.

This adds support for variant chips, however will extend detecting time and image
size. Note that the default chip driver supports the GD chips with product ID
60H.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_SUPPORT_GD_CHIP
children.title: GigaDevice

children.help:
Enable this to support auto detection of Winbond chips if chip vendor not directly
given by ``chip_drv`` member of the chip struct. This adds support for variant
chips, however will extend detecting time.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_SUPPORT_WINBOND_CHIP
children.title: Winbond

children.help:
Enable this to support auto detection of BOYA chips if chip vendor not directly
given by ``chip_drv`` member of the chip struct. This adds support for variant
chips, however will extend detecting time.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_SUPPORT_BOYA_CHIP
children.title: BOYA

children.help:
Enable this to support auto detection of TH chips if chip vendor not directly
given by ``chip_drv`` member of the chip struct. This adds support for variant
chips, however will extend detecting time.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_SUPPORT_TH_CHIP
children.title: TH

children.help:
Enable this to support auto detection of Octal MXIC chips if chip vendor not directly
given by ``chip_drv`` member of the chip struct. This adds support for variant
chips, however will extend detecting time.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_SUPPORT_MXIC_OPI_CHIP
children.title: mxic (opi)

children.help:
This option enables flash read/write operations to encrypted partition/s. This option
is kept enabled irrespective of state of flash encryption feature. However, in case
application is not using flash encryption feature and is in need of some additional
memory from IRAM region (~1KB) then this config can be disabled.
children.name: SPI_FLASH_ENABLE_ENCRYPTED_READ_WRITE
children.title: Enable encrypted partition read/write operations

children.help: Size of the buffer used for constructing the HTTP Upgrade request during connect
children.name: WS_BUFFER_SIZE
children.title: Websocket transport buffer size

children.help:
If enable this option, websocket transport buffer will be freed after connection
succeed to save more heap.
children.name: WS_DYNAMIC_BUFFER
children.title: Using dynamic websocket transport buffer

children.help: Enable support for creating websocket transport.
children.name: WS_TRANSPORT
children.title: Enable Websocket Transport

children.help:
If enabled, the following functions are provided by the VFS component.

stat, link, unlink, rename, utime, access, truncate, rmdir, mkdir,
opendir, closedir, readdir, readdir_r, seekdir, telldir, rewinddir

Filesystem drivers can then be registered to handle these functions
for specific paths.

Disabling this option can save memory when the support for these functions
is not required.
children.name: VFS_SUPPORT_DIR
children.title: Provide directory related functions

children.help:
Select() related functions might produce an inconveniently lot of
debug outputs when one sets the default log level to DEBUG or higher.
It is possible to suppress these debug outputs by enabling this
option.
children.name: VFS_SUPPRESS_SELECT_DEBUG_OUTPUT
children.title: Suppress select() related debug outputs

children.help: If enabled, VFS driver select() callback function will be placed in IRAM.
children.name: VFS_SELECT_IN_RAM
children.title: Make VFS driver select() callbacks IRAM-safe

children.help:
If enabled, select function is provided by the VFS component, and can be used
on peripheral file descriptors (such as UART) and sockets at the same time.

If disabled, the default select implementation will be provided by LWIP for
sockets only.

Disabling this option can reduce code size if support for "select" on UART file
descriptors is not required.
children.name: VFS_SUPPORT_SELECT
children.title: Provide select function

children.help: Disabling this option can save memory when the support for termios.h is not required.
children.name: VFS_SUPPORT_TERMIOS
children.title: Provide termios.h functions

children.help: Define maximum number of virtual filesystems that can be registered.
children.name: VFS_MAX_COUNT
children.title: Maximum Number of Virtual Filesystems

children.help: Define maximum number of host filesystem mount points.
children.name: VFS_SEMIHOSTFS_MAX_MOUNT_POINTS
children.title: Host FS: Maximum number of the host filesystem mount points

children.help: If enabled, /dev/null VFS will be automatically initialized at startup.
children.name: VFS_INITIALIZE_DEV_NULL
children.title: Initialize /dev/null VFS

children.help:
If enabled, the following functions are provided by the VFS component.

open, close, read, write, pread, pwrite, lseek, fstat, fsync, ioctl, fcntl

Filesystem drivers can then be registered to handle these functions
for specific paths.

Disabling this option can save memory when the support for these functions
is not required.

Note that the following functions can still be used with socket file descriptors
when this option is disabled:

close, read, write, ioctl, fcntl.
children.name: VFS_SUPPORT_IO
children.title: Provide basic I/O functions
Configuration for components not included in the build

title: Project configuration for components not included in the build

help:
By enabling this option, ESP-IDF experimental feature options will be visible.

Note you should still enable a certain experimental feature option to use it, and you
should read the corresponding risk warning and known issue list carefully.

Current experimental feature list:

- CONFIG_ESPTOOLPY_FLASHFREQ_120M && CONFIG_ESPTOOLPY_FLASH_SAMPLE_MODE_DTR
- CONFIG_SPIRAM_SPEED_120M && CONFIG_SPIRAM_MODE_OCT
- CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_CACHE_32BIT_ADDR_QUAD_FLASH
- CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_EAP_TLS1_3
- CONFIG_ESP_WIFI_ENABLE_ROAMING_APP
- CONFIG_USB_HOST_EXT_PORT_RESET_ATTEMPTS
- CONFIG_GDMA_ENABLE_WEIGHTED_ARBITRATION
- CONFIG_I3C_MASTER_ENABLED
name: IDF_EXPERIMENTAL_FEATURES
title: Make experimental features visible
